name: Naracoorte
reason: Town with its own Wikivoyage page and listed in the Limestone Coast region page; base for Naracoorte Caves; Sheep's Back Museum in town (rule 1, towns visitors base in).
objection: Wikivoyage's own See entries for the town are thin (museum, gallery); draw is the caves.

name: Beachport
reason: Southaustralia.com names Beachport as a base and lists the Pool of Siloam, Beachport Conservation Park and the jetty area; harbour town second tier.
objection: Only one counted source and the main sights are separate spots.

name: Penola
reason: Coonawarra gateway and Mary MacKillop heritage; no Wikivoyage page and region page only names Coonawarra, the town's own sights (interpretive centre) unverified by a counted source.
objection: For: base for Coonawarra, Mary MacKillop centre. Against: one weak source, cellar doors are not spots.

name: Millicent
reason: Regional hub with the National Trust museum, which southaustralia.com lists (millicent-national-trust-museum); town itself has no guide section.
objection: For: large well-regarded museum and gateway to Canunda. Against: town unnamed by Wikivoyage; museum is the real spot.

name: Port MacDonnell
reason: Southaustralia.com names Port MacDonnell as a stay base on the Limestone Coast; fishing village on Southern Ocean Drive (second-tier harbour town).
objection: Single source; no named sights on the sources I opened.

name: Southend
reason: Southaustralia.com's Limestone Coast beaches section names Southend (listed as an attraction with boating facilities); beach village on Rivoli Bay.
objection: One counted source; Wikivoyage's Southend page is Southend-on-Sea, not this place.

name: Bordertown
reason: Dukes Highway stopover; southaustralia.com lists Bordertown Wildlife Park (white kangaroos) and Recreation Lake; the town itself has no own guide section.
objection: For: white kangaroos are a quirky roadside draw. Against: that draw is the park, not the town; judge the wildlife park as its own place.

name: Tantanoola
reason: Village with no visitor source naming anything to see beyond the caves, which are a separate candidate (Tantanoola Caves); the Tiger is a pub/stuffed animal.
objection: Tantanoola Tiger is a quirky icon, but it lacks a counted source.

name: Mundulla
reason: Dukes Highway village with no counted source naming anything to see.
objection: Could have a mineral springs/heritage mention I did not find.

name: Lucindale
reason: Farming village; no counted source names a draw (Big Heath is a separate park).
objection: Small chance a guide lists it as a stop.

name: Padthaway
reason: Wine locality: no counted source; cellar doors and an estate operator are not spots (brief: hold the winery line).
objection: The Padthaway Estate homestead is a heritage estate.

name: Carpenter Rocks
reason: Fishing village with no counted source; Cape Banks lighthouse not verified; Canunda covers the coast.
objection: Cape Banks Lighthouse and fishing harbour might be a stop.

name: Nora Creina
reason: Bay and cliffs between Robe and Beachport but no counted source found naming it as a visit; search only found general beach articles.
objection: Scenic curving bay on Southern Ocean Drive; could be second-tier headland if a guide names it.

name: Cape Jaffa
reason: Locality; the Cape Jaffa Lighthouse is a Kingston SE sight per Wikivoyage (listed under Kingston), not a distinct place at Cape Jaffa; duplicate of the Kingston lighthouse.
objection: The lighthouse was originally offshore at Cape Jaffa and Cape Jaffa has a wine/ marina community.

name: Nangwarry
reason: Forestry village; the museum has no counted source.
objection: Nangwarry Forestry Museum may be open to the public.

name: Cave Garden / Thugi
reason: Visitmountgambier.com.au page: walk down into the city-centre sinkhole or view from platform; Wikivoyage mentions Cave Garden in Mount Gambier; permanent public place (rule 2).
objection: Short visit, ~20 min, in town beside the arts centre.

name: Little Blue Lake
reason: Southaustralia.com lists it as a free attraction and visitmountgambier.com.au page describes swimming in a sinkhole via pontoon; second-tier swim spot.
objection: Two sources but a short stop and seasonal swimming; private land access.

name: Kilsby Sinkhole
reason: Southaustralia.com ($15) and visitmountgambier.com.au page: a dive/snorkel site with above-water tours with a certified guide; entry is operator-managed.
objection: For: one of Australia's significant dive sites, in two counted sources. Against: it is a guided/operator experience, certification needed.

name: Valley Lake / Ketla Malpi
reason: Visitmountgambier.com.au page: second crater lake with grassed area, playground, BBQs and the conservation park walks; Wikivoyage also names Valley Lake with picnic grounds and trails.
objection: Near duplicate of the Blue Lake crater precinct; family picnic stop.

name: Mount Gambier (volcano)
reason: Duplicate of the Blue Lake/Mount Gambier crater precinct: the volcano is the ground under the lakes and lookouts already kept.
objection: The Centenary Tower lookout could be a spot of its own.

name: Mount Schank
reason: Wikivoyage Mount Gambier (see list) and visitmountgambier.com.au: 900 m signposted walk to the crater rim with 360-degree views, state heritage area.
objection: Moderate climb; descent into the crater not recommended.

name: Fossil Cave
reason: No counted source; a Naracoorte-area cave not offered on the Naracoorte Caves tour list.
objection: May be part of the World Heritage fossil site.

name: Mount Gambier Lady Nelson Visitor Centre
reason: Visitor centre with ship replica; Wikivoyage calls the walk not really worth the money; a centre, not a draw (rule 2).
objection: Giant boat is a quirky roadside icon.

name: Old Mount Gambier Gaol
reason: Wikivoyage lists it under Sleep (accommodation in the old gaol); historic gaol tours are offered but I found no See entry.
objection: For: heritage gaol. Against: accommodation business, one source.

name: Riddoch Arts and Cultural Centre
reason: Gallery and civic cultural centre; no counted source.
objection: Cave Garden beside it is covered separately.

name: Mount Gambier Volcano Movie (Kings Theatre)
reason: Operator screening of a film (rule: operator, recurring show).
objection: Visitmountgambier lists it daily.

name: Aberdour Conservation Park
reason: Low-profile scrub park with no counted source.
objection: Park could have walking trails.

name: Mount Burr
reason: Forest area village, no counted source.
objection: Pine forest drives.

name: Mount Muirhead
reason: Hill with no counted source.
objection: Might have lookouts.

name: Ewens Ponds
reason: Parks SA page: spring-fed limestone ponds to snorkel or dive, with walking trails; Ramsar-type natural feature (snorkelling closed 1 Sep-30 Nov).
objection: Snorkelling closed three months a year; permit needed to dive.

name: Piccaninnie Ponds
reason: Parks SA: immersive water activities closed until further notice; the park remains open for a walk along the beach to see springs and boardwalks.
objection: For: well-known dive site and beach walk. Against: the main draw is closed; only a walk remains.

name: Tantanoola Caves
reason: Parks SA page: one of South Australia's most impressive caves, free park entry, fees for cave entry; tours are the draw.
objection: Smaller, single-cave visit.

name: Canunda National Park
reason: Wikivoyage Limestone Coast lists it in Other destinations; Parks SA: cliffs, surf beaches, dunes, walking.
objection: None serious; 4WD only for some sections.

name: Little Dip Conservation Park
reason: Wikivoyage Robe lists it as a See; Parks SA: dunes, lakes, coastal mallee, 4WD.
objection: Low views, many parts 4WD.

name: Beachport Conservation Park
reason: Parks SA: limestone cliffs, middens, Woolley Lake walking trail with ocean views; southaustralia.com lists it.
objection: Part of the Beachport coast; moderate overlap with Pool of Siloam drive.

name: Victoria Fossil Cave
reason: Naracoorte Caves site names it as a tour cave (the main World Heritage tour); but it is inside Naracoorte Caves National Park.
objection: For: the headline cave tour, separately ticketed. Against: part of a larger spot (rule 3).

name: Alexandra Cave
reason: Tour cave inside Naracoorte Caves National Park: part of the larger spot (rule 3).
objection: Separate tour and ticket.

name: Blanche Cave
reason: Cave inside Naracoorte Caves National Park, same bat-centre tour as Bat Centre: part of the larger spot.
objection: Distinct tour.

name: Wonambi Fossil Centre
reason: Interpretive centre inside Naracoorte Caves National Park: part of the larger spot.
objection: Separate fossil displays.

name: Stick-Tomato Cave
reason: Adventure cave inside Naracoorte Caves National Park, an operator-style adventure tour: part of the larger spot.
objection: Bookable tour of its own.

name: Naracoorte Caves Adventure Caving
reason: Operator experience inside Naracoorte Caves National Park, not a place.
objection: Park's own guided programme.

name: Bat Centre, Naracoorte Caves
reason: Duplicate of Blanche Cave inside Naracoorte Caves National Park.
objection: Bat viewing is a headline wildlife experience.

name: Sheep's Back Museum
reason: Wikivoyage See entry: local history and woolgrowing museum and visitor centre, $8 entry; open daily.
objection: For: open museum with counted listing. Against: local museum, one source.

name: Naracoorte Regional Art Gallery
reason: Wikivoyage describes it as 'just another art gallery'; local gallery, one source.
objection: Open to the public.

name: Bool Lagoon
reason: Southaustralia.com attraction page: Ramsar wetland with 500 m boardwalk, brolga and 150 bird species; seasonal water (rule 4 ok).
objection: Often dry; boardwalk can end far from water.

name: Hacks Lagoon
reason: Duplicate of Bool Lagoon: southaustralia.com lists them as one attraction (Bool Lagoon Game Reserve and Hacks Lagoon Conservation Park).
objection: Separate conservation park.

name: Padthaway Estate
reason: Winery/estate operator (brief: only landmark estates a guide singles out).
objection: Historic homestead estate.

name: Naracoorte Woodlands
reason: Protected woodland, no counted source.
objection: Close to Naracoorte.

name: Mount Monster Conservation Park
reason: Parks SA page and Wikivoyage Keith: unusual granite outcrop 12 km south of Keith, picnics, hikes, wildflowers.
objection: For: two counted sources. Against: low-profile park, short stop.

name: Penola Conservation Park
reason: Low-profile park with no counted source.
objection: Could have a bushwalk.

name: Coorong National Park (South East end)
reason: outside the region: belongs to sa-murray (Murray River, Lakes and Coorong); the Coorong is covered there.
objection: Southern end lies in the Limestone Coast.

name: Ngarkat Conservation Park
reason: outside the region: belongs to the Murray Mallee region; no counted source here.
objection: Near Tatiara border.

name: Penguin Island (Robe)
reason: Island penguin colony reached only by guided tour (operator); no public access otherwise.
objection: Little penguin colony is a genuine wildlife draw.

name: Baudin Rocks
reason: Offshore rocks conservation park with no visitor access or counted source.
objection: Seabird colony.

name: Lake Bonney SE
reason: No counted source; lake and wind farm only.
objection: Lakeside camping.

name: Lake George (South Australia)
reason: No counted source.
objection: Waterbird lake.

name: Lake Frome (south east)
reason: No counted source.
objection: Wetland.

name: Robe Lighthouse
reason: Wikivoyage Robe lists it (a 1972 concrete lighthouse, 'not historic') alongside the Cape Dombey Obelisk (1855); coast viewpoint at Robe.
objection: For: Obelisk is a coastal landmark. Against: the guide itself downplays it; short stop.
